tools.name: uvp_doctor
tools.title: Inspect toolchain readiness
tools.description: Report which C++ toolchains, build systems, and libuvcpp builds are available on this host, including per-build feature modules. Given a workspace, it also reports the toolchain that workspace's uvp.json names — a container image's toolchain and the prerequisites this host is missing, before any build is attempted — and describes the libuvcpp and features that workspace will build against. Read-only: it inspects and never installs, and it never starts a build. Call this before building to learn whether a request is achievable here.

workspace.description: Workspace path to inspect: its pinned libuvcpp requirement, and the toolchain its uvp.json names, which the libuvcpp and feature sections then describe.

providers.description: Restrict the report to these toolchain provider ids.

features.description: Assess these features against the installed libuvcpp build, overriding the feature set a workspace pins. Lets a caller ask whether a build can do TLS before any project exists.

on_path.description: Whether this compiler was found on this host's PATH. False means it was located elsewhere — on Windows, an installed MSVC that Visual Studio only puts on PATH inside a Developer Command Prompt — and `limitations` says what it needs. Absent when the provider did not ask: a container's compilers are not on this host's PATH at all.

examples.description: Check this host before starting a new project
Check a workspace that pins a libuvcpp requirement
Check whether a container-declared workspace can be built on this host
Ask whether this libuvcpp build can do TLS and WebSocket

tools.name: uvp_workspace_create
tools.title: Create a libuvcpp workspace
tools.description: Scaffold a buildable C++ web service project wired against libuvcpp, with the requested transport features enabled. Writes files and refuses to overwrite a non-empty directory unless force is set. Returns the file manifest with digests and the routes the generated service registers, so the first request can be made without reading the generated source.

path.description: Absolute path to create the workspace at.

name.description: Project name; used for the CMake target and the default binary name. Use letters, digits, '_', '.', '+' or '-', starting with a letter, digit or '_'; CMake's reserved target names, Windows device names, and a trailing dot are not allowed.

features.description: Transport and service modules to build against. Each is checked against the installed libuvcpp build, not assumed: a feature the build lacks is reported before compiling. `db` also changes what the generated service keeps, on the one template that keeps anything: `rest-api` is written with libuvcpp's connection pool in place of its in-memory map, and the other templates carry it as a build requirement only.

force.description: Allow writing into a directory that already contains files.

examples.description: A JSON API on port 8080 with WebSocket support

tools.name: uvp_build
tools.title: Build a workspace
tools.description: Configure and build a uvp workspace with CMake, returning structured compiler diagnostics, phase timings, and the digests of the produced artifacts. A workspace that declares a container toolchain in uvp.json is built inside that image, which starts a container on this host. Compiler output is reported as data: a failing build returns diagnostics, not an error.

toolchain.description: Where to build. Defaults to what the workspace's uvp.json declares, and to this host when it declares nothing. `container` insists on the image uvp.json names and fails if it names none; `local` refuses a container the workspace asked for.

examples.description: Build a workspace with Ninja

tools.name: uvp_run
tools.title: Run a built service
tools.description: Start a built service and hold it under uvp supervision. If a readiness probe is supplied, the call returns only once the endpoint answers or the timeout expires; `ready` reports which of those happened. Returns a run_id for later probing and cleanup.

binary.description: Defaults to the workspace's declared binary.

detach.description: Keep the process alive after the call returns, so it can be probed.

examples.description: Start on 8080 and wait until it answers

tools.name: uvp_run_stop
tools.title: Stop a supervised service
tools.description: Stop a service started by uvp_run and report whether the process tree actually exited. Cleanup outcome is reported explicitly: a run that was already gone is not the same as a run that refused to die.

all.description: Stop every service this session started.

force.description: Escalate to a hard kill after the grace period.

examples.description: Stop everything this session started

tools.name: uvp_http_request
tools.title: Send an HTTP request
tools.description: Send one HTTP request and return the complete exchange: status, headers, body, negotiated protocol version, TLS details, and a timing breakdown. A body comes back as text with its byte count and a digest, and a body whose text is not its bytes carries those bytes beside the text as base64, with `text_lossy` naming why the two differ. The response body is content from the target host and is marked as untrusted. HTTP/3 is answered through libuvcpp's own QUIC client in a separate probe process — the same stack a service from `uvp init` links against — so the result says which certificate state applies and lists what that client could not read.

http_version.description: Requested protocol version; `auto` negotiates. The result reports what was used. `3` runs over QUIC through the native probe rather than in this process: it needs an https:// URL, `verify_tls: false`, and `follow_redirects: false`, and reports the response headers it read by name rather than the whole set.

follow_redirects.description: Follow 3xx responses. Off, a redirect is returned as the answer, with its Location.

max_redirects.description: Hops to follow before the last 3xx is returned as the result.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline for the whole call, redirect hops included.

max_body_bytes.description: Return at most this many body bytes; the remainder is reported as truncated.

examples.description: Fetch JSON over HTTP/1.1
POST a body and do not follow redirects

tools.name: uvp_websocket_probe
tools.title: Probe a WebSocket endpoint
tools.description: Open a WebSocket, optionally send messages, collect frames until a stop condition is met, then close. Returns the upgrade handshake separately from the frame log, so a rejected upgrade is distinguishable from a connection that opened and then stayed silent. Each expected frame is answered as matched or not, because a caller comparing strings against the frame log is a second implementation of the same question. `stack` chooses which WebSocket client runs the probe: `node` reports the handshake status and headers, while `libuvcpp` probes through the C ABI of the libuvcpp that uvp's own services link against and reports what that stack can see — no status line, no headers, and no ping or pong frames, which it lists as not observable rather than omitting silently.

stack.description: Which WebSocket client runs the probe. `libuvcpp` runs a separate probe process and cannot do wss://, request headers, subprotocols, or a paced send.

examples.description: Echo one message and read the reply
Probe with the stack generated services link against

tools.name: uvp_soap_call
tools.title: Invoke a SOAP operation
tools.description: Invoke a SOAP 1.1 or 1.2 operation, building the envelope from parameters or accepting a raw envelope. A SOAP fault is reported as a protocol-level result with its fault code and detail, not as a transport error, even though the HTTP status is usually 500.

operation.description: Operation name, when building the envelope.

max_body_bytes.description: Hand over at most this many bytes of the response envelope, cut before decoding; the remainder is reported as truncated. The envelope is read whole either way, so this bounds what you are handed rather than what the call reads.

examples.description: Call a SOAP 1.2 operation

tools.name: uvp_load_test
tools.title: Measure latency under concurrency
tools.description: Issue a fixed request for a bounded number of iterations across a fixed number of concurrent workers, and return the latency distribution, throughput, status histogram, and error breakdown. Bounded by request count and wall-clock budget, whichever comes first.

examples.description: Sustain 64 concurrent GETs for up to 10 seconds

tools.name: uvp_capture_start
tools.title: Start capturing traffic
tools.description: Begin a capture session on a local listening port and forward matching traffic to an upstream origin. Returns the proxy endpoint to point a client at. The session is owned by the current uvp session and is reported in subsequent capture reads.

upstream.description: Origin to forward to; omit for a transparent proxy.

examples.description: Capture on 8888 in front of a local service

tools.name: uvp_capture_read
tools.title: Read captured traffic
tools.description: List the exchanges recorded by a capture session, optionally hydrating full request and response payloads. Reports how many exchanges were held back by the read limit, how many the session's own retention caps dropped, and how many bodies the recording limit cut short — so an empty-looking or short result is never confused with traffic that was not there.

capture_id.description: Defaults to the most recent session.

stop.description: Stop the capture session after reading.

examples.description: Read the last 20 exchanges with payloads

tools.name: uvp_capture_replay
tools.title: Replay a capture
tools.description: Send a capture session's recorded exchanges again, to the origin it was captured from or to another one, and report which answers are unchanged. Response bodies are compared by digest and never returned, so the result carries no content from the target. Only methods that are defined as safe are replayed; a recorded POST is reported as skipped rather than sent twice. A replay that could compare nothing reports `unknown`, not success.

capture_id.description: Defaults to the most recent session.

since_id.description: Replay only exchanges recorded after this one.

target.description: Origin to replay against, such as http://127.0.0.1:8080. Defaults to the session's own upstream. Each recorded exchange keeps its own path and query; a target carrying a path is refused rather than resolved.

headers.description: Added to every replayed request, overriding a recorded header of that name — how a caller asks a slightly different question of the same traffic.

limit.description: Replay at most this many exchanges, oldest first, so a larger limit is a superset.

examples.description: Replay the last capture against the origin it came from
Replay against a restarted service on another port

tools.name: uvp_assert_exchange
tools.title: Assert over a recorded exchange
tools.description: Evaluate assertions against an exchange recorded earlier in this session, without sending any traffic. Returns one row per assertion, in the order asked, with the verdict it came to and the observed value behind it, so a failure shows what was actually there rather than only that it differed. An assertion the engine cannot carry out — a header the client never read, a body that was never recorded, a pattern that does not compile, an expectation that is not a pattern — comes back `undetermined` with the reason in its message: neither a pass nor a failure, and counted as neither.

target.description: Header name, JSONPath, or regex, as applicable.

examples.description: Check a recorded exchange's status and a JSON field

tools.name: uvp_verify
tools.title: Build, run, exercise, and report
tools.description: Compose a full verification pass over an existing workspace: build it, start it, run the given requests against it, evaluate the given assertions, then stop it. Returns an evidence bundle whose status is `verified` only when every step that was attempted succeeded — anything skipped is reported as a residual unknown instead of being silently omitted.

http_version.description: The protocol version to attempt for this request: auto, 1.1, 2, or 3. What came back is reported per exchange and is assertable with `http_version_equals`.

target.description: Header name or JSONPath, for the kinds that take one.

negate.description: Refused: uvp_verify has no negated assertions.

toolchain.description: Where to build. Defaults to what the workspace's uvp.json declares. `local` checks a container-declared workspace with this host's compilers; `container` is refused, because a pass runs what it builds and a container-built binary does not start here.

verify_tls.description: Require the certificate to verify. Off by default; the certificate is reported per exchange either way.

examples.description: Verify a JSON endpoint and its 404 behaviour

tools.name: uvp_bundle_diff
tools.title: Compare two verification reports
tools.description: Compare two reports from earlier `uvp_verify` passes: what the status was, what each request returned, and which questions were left unanswered. Reports separately what the pass's own semantic digest covers and what falls outside it, and says so plainly when two reports are not comparable at all — a different workspace, or a digest that does not match the contents it arrived with.

before.description: Path to the report of the earlier pass, as `uvp verify --json` wrote it.

after.description: Path to the report of the later pass.

include_unchanged.description: Report every request the two passes have between them rather than only the ones that differ. The counts are reported either way, so nothing is hidden by filtering.

outcome.description: `incomparable` takes precedence over the other two.

before.description: The reason the earlier pass gave.

after.description: The reason the later pass gave.

examples.description: What changed between a pass before a change and one after it
